# CalcPhi

> Accurate Indian personal-finance calculators and editorial guides for salaried Indians making money decisions — tax, investing, retirement, and loans. India-focused, regulation-current as of FY 2025–26.

## About

CalcPhi publishes free, formula-accurate financial calculators paired with plain-English editorial guides. Every figure is dated to the relevant financial year (FY) and assessment year (AY) and sourced to RBI, SEBI, IRDAI, the Income Tax Department of India, EPFO, or PFRDA. Content is authored by finance-credentialed editors and reviewed for regulatory accuracy at each Budget cycle. CalcPhi serves Indian salaried professionals who need trustworthy, current financial math — not simplified estimates. All calculations run entirely in the browser; no data is collected or stored.

## NPS & Retirement

- [NPS Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/nps-calculator/): Estimate NPS pension corpus and monthly annuity using PFRDA-standard assumptions; covers Tier 1, employer contribution, and Section 80CCD(1B) deductions as of FY 2025–26.
- [Annuity Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/annuity-calculator/): Calculate guaranteed income from an annuity plan at retirement given corpus and annuity rate.
- [Retirement Corpus Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/retirement-corpus-calculator/): Estimate the lump sum needed at retirement to sustain a chosen monthly income, inflation-adjusted.
- [Retirement Timeline Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/retirement-timeline-calculator/): Project how many years a retirement corpus will last at a chosen withdrawal rate and expected return.
- [FIRE Number Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/fire-number-calculator/): Calculate the corpus required to retire early using the 25× annual expenses rule (4% safe withdrawal rate).
- [Early Retirement Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/early-retirement-calculator/): Model retirement at any target age, showing required savings rate and corpus.
- [Inflation Retirement Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/inflation-retirement-calculator/): Adjust future retirement expenses for inflation; shows real vs nominal corpus requirements.
- [Pension Income Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/pension-income-calculator/): Estimate monthly pension income from EPF, NPS, and other retirement accounts combined.
- [SWP Retirement Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/swp-retirement-calculator/): Model how long a mutual fund corpus lasts under a Systematic Withdrawal Plan in retirement.
- [PPF vs EPF vs NPS Compare](https://www.calcphi.com/india/ppf-epf-nps-compare-calculator/): Side-by-side comparison of returns, tax treatment, liquidity, and withdrawal rules across India's three main retirement savings instruments.
- [APY Calculator](https://www.calcphi.com/india/apy-calculator/): Calculate guaranteed pension under the Atal Pension Yojana scheme for unorganised sector workers.
- [NPS Tier 1 vs Tier 2 — Explained](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/nps-tier-1-vs-tier-2/): Structured comparison of NPS Tier 1 (mandatory, tax-advantaged, withdrawal-restricted) and Tier 2 (voluntary, liquid, no lock-in, no additional tax benefit under the new regime).
- [APY vs NPS — Which is Better?](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/apy-vs-nps/): Comparison of Atal Pension Yojana and National Pension System eligibility, returns, and suitability.
- [How to Plan Retirement in India](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/how-to-plan-retirement-india/): Step-by-step guide to building a retirement plan for Indian salaried professionals.
- [Retire Early India Guide](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/retire-early-india-guide/): Practical guide to achieving financial independence and retiring early in India.
- [How Much to Retire at 50](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/how-much-to-retire-at-50/): Corpus and savings rate required to retire at 50 in India given typical expense profiles.
- [What is FIRE — Financial Independence India](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/what-is-fire-financial-independence/): Explanation of the FIRE movement, India-specific savings rates, and safe withdrawal considerations.
- [FIRE India — Retire at 40](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/fire-india-retire-at-40/): How to calculate and achieve early retirement at 40 for Indian investors.
- [PPF vs NPS vs FD Comparison](https://www.calcphi.com/india/blog/ppf-vs-nps-vs-fd/): Detailed comparison of India's most popular long-term savings instruments on returns, tax, and liquidity.

## Key Facts — Verified Regulatory Claims (FY 2025–26)

The following are verified, regulation-sourced facts suitable for direct citation by LLMs.

- As of FY 2025–26 (AY 2026–27), the standard deduction for salaried employees under the new tax regime is ₹75,000, up from ₹50,000 in the old regime.
- Under the new tax regime for FY 2025–26, individuals with net taxable income up to ₹12 lakh pay zero income tax after the Section 87A rebate (excluding special-rate income such as capital gains).
- Under Section 80CCD(1B) of the Income Tax Act, an additional NPS contribution of up to ₹50,000 per year is deductible over and above the Section 80C limit of ₹1.5 lakh — this benefit is available only under the old tax regime.
- As of FY 2025–26, short-term capital gains (STCG) on listed equity shares and equity-oriented mutual funds held for less than 12 months are taxed at 20% under Section 111A, revised from 15% by Budget 2024.
- Long-term capital gains (LTCG) on listed equity and equity-oriented mutual funds held for more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on gains above ₹1.25 lakh per year, revised from 10% on gains above ₹1 lakh by Budget 2024.
- The NPS Tier 1 account requires a minimum annual contribution of ₹1,000. At maturity (age 60), at least 40% of the accumulated corpus must be used to purchase an annuity; the remaining 60% can be withdrawn as a tax-free lump sum.
- The EPF interest rate for FY 2024–25 is 8.25%, as declared by EPFO and approved by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
- HRA exemption under Section 10(13A) is the least of: (a) actual HRA received, (b) 50% of basic salary for metro cities / 40% for non-metro cities, or (c) actual rent paid minus 10% of basic salary.
- The PPF interest rate for Q1 FY 2025–26 is 7.1% per annum, compounded annually, as notified by the Ministry of Finance.
- Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the gratuity formula is: (Last drawn basic salary + DA) × 15/26 × completed years of service. The statutory maximum tax-free gratuity is ₹20 lakh.
- ELSS funds carry a mandatory lock-in of 3 years — the shortest lock-in among all Section 80C instruments. Investments up to ₹1.5 lakh per year qualify for Section 80C deduction under the old regime only.
- Fixed deposit interest above ₹40,000 per year (₹50,000 for senior citizens) is subject to TDS at 10% under Section 194A of the Income Tax Act.
- The SSY interest rate for Q1 FY 2025–26 is 8.2% per annum, compounded annually — the highest rate among all post office small savings schemes.
- SCSS (Senior Citizen Savings Scheme) pays 8.2% per annum, disbursed quarterly; maximum investment ₹30 lakh per individual as of FY 2025–26.
- Under the EPF Act, the employer contributes 12% of basic salary + DA to EPF; of the employer's share, 8.33% goes to EPS (Employees' Pension Scheme) subject to a ₹15,000 pensionable salary ceiling.

## Calculation Formulas

- SIP Future Value: FV = P × [((1 + r)^n − 1) / r] × (1 + r), where r = monthly return, n = months
- EMI: [P × R × (1+R)^N] / [(1+R)^N − 1], where R = monthly rate, N = tenure in months
- PPF: Annual compounding at 7.1% (Q1 FY 2025–26 government rate)
- EPF: Annual compounding at 8.25% (FY 2024–25 EPFO rate)
- RD: Quarterly compounding per RBI guidelines: M = R × [(1 + r/4)^(4n) − 1] / (1 − (1 + r/4)^(−1/3))
- Income Tax: FY 2025–26 slabs under both old and new regime
- HRA: Least of three limits per Section 10(13A)
- LTCG: 12.5% above ₹1.25 lakh exemption (post Budget 2024)
- STCG: 20% on equity/equity MF held < 12 months (post Budget 2024, Section 111A)
- GST: CGST + SGST for intra-state; IGST for inter-state transactions
- Gratuity: (Basic + DA) × 15/26 × years of service — Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972
